decisions.rationale: The evidence says that the desire to resolve inconsistencies led to the development of quantum mechanics and describes the revolution as a shift; it does not state that the quantum revolution caused that development.
The Pauli exclusion principle imposes the stated restriction that electrons in an atom cannot share the same set of quantum numbers, supporting a CONSTRAINS relation to electrons.
The evidence identifies quantum electrodynamics as the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force, but does not support the added claim that it developed into quantum field theory.
The evidence says superfluidity is a phenomenon explained using quantum mechanics, not that superfluidity is an illustrative instance of quantum mechanics.
The evidence identifies the electron microscope as an application of quantum mechanics, but does not explicitly establish the stronger ENABLES commitment that quantum mechanics makes it possible.
The evidence relates quantum tunneling to the operation of a simple light switch and electron penetration of an oxide barrier, not directly to the transistor endpoint.
The evidence explicitly states that light passing through the two slits produces an interference pattern, matching the stated CAUSES direction and endpoints.
The evidence explicitly describes the Standard Model as the quantum field theory, supporting its classification as a quantum field theory.
The evidence explicitly states that the correspondence principle requires quantum theory to converge to classical limits, supporting a constraint on quantum mechanics.
